classification: accepted-design normative conflict discovered during application revalidation

falsifier.d0039Rule: Mutating managementRequestId is m1:<target lifecycleGeneration>, exactly predecessor + 1.
falsifier.d0027Rule: Every product-side lifecycle mutation advances lifecycleGeneration, while one stable managementRequestId may own a crash-safe multi-phase management transaction.
contradiction: D0027 compatible package update/rollback uses one stable managementRequestId, elects a draining lifecycleGeneration before quiescence, then elects a distinct final active lifecycleGeneration after readiness.
D0027 normal uninstall uses one stable managementRequestId, elects an uninstall-owned draining lifecycleGeneration, then a distinct final revoked lifecycleGeneration.
Therefore one stable managementRequestId cannot simultaneously encode the final target lifecycleGeneration and equal the original predecessor lifecycleGeneration + 1 for these accepted transitions.

facts: management lifecycle journal binds one stable managementRequestId per transaction
every new product-side lifecycle mutation advances lifecycleGeneration
base stop/start each elect a new lifecycle generation
normal uninstall requires draining generation then final revoked generation
beginPackageActivation allocates drainingLifecycleGeneration and finalLifecycleGeneration under one managementRequestId
commitPackageActivation applies finalLifecycleGeneration under that same managementRequestId
beginInstallableAgentUninstall allocates draining lifecycleGeneration under one managementRequestId
completeInstallableAgentUninstall allocates a new final revoked lifecycleGeneration under the same managementRequestId
